value: Law of 21 September 2006 on the lease of dwellings (consolidated version).
source_publisher: Legilux (Journal officiel du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)

value: Letting a dwelling may not yield the landlord an annual income above 5 percent of the capital invested in the dwelling (revalued); for a furnished dwelling a furniture supplement of at most 1.5 percent of the total furniture invoices per month may be added (art. 3).
source_publisher: Legilux (Journal officiel du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)

value: The parties may agree a rental guarantee not exceeding two months of rent; a written and adversarial inventory of the premises must be signed by the day the tenant takes possession, and the landlord may not refuse a bank guarantee as the form of security (art. 5(2)).
source_publisher: Legilux (Journal officiel du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)

value: A lease must be in writing on pain of nullity, stating the parties, start date, premises, rent without charges, charges, any furniture supplement, any guarantee and the possibility to refer rent disputes to the rent commission (art. 5(1)).
source_publisher: Legilux (Journal officiel du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)

value: A lease that ends for any reason is extended for an indefinite term unless the landlord needs the premises for self or a relative up to the third degree, the tenant fails obligations, or there are other serious and legitimate grounds (art. 12(2)).
source_publisher: Legilux (Journal officiel du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)

value: For landlord own use or use by a relative the notice period is six months, by written reasoned registered letter; the tenant may ask the justice of the peace to extend it within three months (art. 12(3)).
source_publisher: Legilux (Journal officiel du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)
